evidenceRoutes.source: Taiwan Ratings corporate default and transition studies
evidenceRoutes.coverage: annual rating transition/default research with historical Taiwan corporate series
evidenceRoutes.finding: The 1999-2023 table shows many zero-default years and a long-run weighted average default rate around 0.3%, confirming rare-event sparsity within the rated universe.
evidenceRoutes.limitation: Rated-universe defaults are not a complete Taiwan listed-company distress universe; coverage and rating selection create selection bias.

evidenceRoutes.source: Taiwan Ratings 2023 corporate default and transition study
evidenceRoutes.finding: Recent years in the displayed table frequently record zero corporate defaults while downgrade frequencies vary.
evidenceRoutes.limitation: Annual summary is not an issuer-level recovery cash-flow panel.
Notice type must be classified before use; it cannot be automatically equated with corporate-bond issuer credit default.

evidenceRoutes.finding: Bankruptcy and court-confirmed restructuring are among formal listing-termination conditions.
evidenceRoutes.limitation: Rules define event semantics but do not by themselves supply a historical issuer-event/recovery panel.

rarityAudit.ratedUniverseObservation: Corporate default is a rare event in Taiwan Ratings annual history; many years show zero defaults.
rarityAudit.modelingImplication: Naive classification accuracy can look high by predicting no default. Calibration, rare-event metrics and explicit class imbalance handling are mandatory.
rarityAudit.selectionImplication: Using only currently listed or currently rated firms creates survivorship/coverage bias.
rarityAudit.recoveryImplication: Recovery/LGD needs creditor seniority, collateral, restructuring/liquidation process and realized recovery timing; rating default counts alone are insufficient.

prohibitedShortcuts: Do not label every delisting as credit default.
Do not label every TPEx market default notice as issuer default without event-type classification.
Do not infer recovery from post-default equity price.
Do not set a universal recovery percentage and call it Taiwan evidence.
Do not train only on surviving/rated firms and call the result a Taiwan default model.
Do not treat distance-to-default output as observed PD.

maturityDecision.rationale: Official source routes and rare-event/selection-bias semantics are established, but a reproducible issuer-level Taiwan default/restructuring/recovery panel including delisted/defaulted cases has not yet been built. L3 data-feasibility is therefore not proven.

next: Build a classified issuer-level event ledger separating bankruptcy, restructuring, bond-payment default, delayed payment, covenant breach, trading default and non-credit delisting.

Preregister rare-event metrics, horizon/default-barrier choices and censoring treatment before any model/outcome test.
